correctness.rationale: For every \(s>0\) and all Borel mean-half laws on \([0,1]\), the exact squared scalar multiplier is \(g_s(t)=(1-s+st)^2/(1+st)^2\). Three independently factored global affine lower supports prove the infimum and uniqueness in all three stiffness regimes, including both endpoint thresholds. The scalar all-step identity follows from stage independence. CHECK.py confirms the exact algebraic identities and finite illustrative cases; the universal sign inequalities are proved in RESULT.md rather than inferred from enumeration.

value.rationale: The full stage-law design under a prescribed mean is a motivated stability question for randomized implicit Runge-Kutta: it determines the best mean-square damping achievable without changing nominal stage centering. The unusual transition between endpoint two-point sampling, asymmetric interior-to-endpoint two-point sampling, and deterministic midpoint is sharp. At \(s=1\) an asymmetric random stage strictly beats deterministic midpoint (\(7/64\) versus \(1/9\)), while above \(2/\sqrt3\) randomization cannot help. The result is not merely a trivial restatement of a fixed-law stability integral and has explicit limitations.
